correctness.rationale: Exact identification of dyadic holes with constant binary blocks gives the weighted run decomposition for every finite horizon. The alternating-run generating function identifies the unique root of a primitive 2(k-1)-state transfer matrix. For lambda>1, both factors strictly decrease; the product is >1 at lambda=3/2 and <1 at 2. Differentiating the product with respect to x=p(1-p) gives a manifestly negative numerator c[(c-2S)(lambda^2-lambda)-S lambda]. The uniform expansion lambda=2-O(2^-k) yields gamma=2^-k B(p)+O(k4^-k) and B(1/2)/B(0)=4/3. A checker gives 160 exact-rational independent finite-horizon equalities and 36 numerical Perron comparisons. No finite computation is used in place of the all-depth proof.

originality.rationale: The all-depth, strictly bias-ordered annealed escape theorem and the exact limiting 4/3 enhancement were not found in the inspected sources. General averaged transfer matrices (2012) and deterministic forbidden-word correlation methods (2019) already imply existence of finite spectral calculations and are credited as framework, not claimed new. The quenched 2021 theory computes a different order of averaging. The proof of the explicit strict optimality and its uniform rare-hole constant requires a run-renewal algebraic comparison beyond merely invoking Perron-Frobenius.

value.rationale: The iid choice bias is a natural constrained escape-design variable when each candidate hole has the same size. The theorem proves, for every depth k>=3, a unique optimal bias and a sharp rare-hole gain by a universal nontrivial factor 4/3, not just a numerical instance or a routine restatement of the existence of escape rates. It also separates annealed optimization from arbitrary-schedule control and quenched pressure, identifying the exact mathematical applicability.
